## Conformance stance

MIL-STD-3071 §1.5 (p.1): *"This document does not define test procedures that verify compliance with this standard."* No attestation or report format is prescribed anywhere in the standard. This report's spine is the A.8.7 topic × usage × condition matrix (Required / Conditional-on-10-named-conditions / Optional — Tables B.1 p.64 / B.2 p.65), plus the D.4/D.5 "Conformance testing will verify..." categories (participation vs. DeviceInfo, extensibility, keys, bounded values, units, QoS interoperability).

**This gate checks IDL type-catalogue coverage, not runtime publish-wiring coverage.** `tms-coverage.json` records, for every topic, whether the descriptor factory (`tools/tms-idl-codegen`) parsed an IDL `@topic` annotation and produced a shaped Rust type for it — it carries no field for whether `bin-rpi` actually publishes/subscribes that topic at runtime today. That second, currently-manual axis is tracked in `docs/tms-compliance.md` and mirrored (as of this pass) in `compliance/oscal/component-definition.json`'s `bin-rpi` component.

## Documented adaptations (project-wide, not defects)

- **Transport**: MQTT+JSON, not DDS/XCDR2/RTPS/UDP/IPv6 domain 0 (D.1-D.3) — the IDL is used only as the schema-shape oracle.
- **JSON key casing**: snake_case wire keys vs. IDL camelCase members — spec-silent (the real DDS wire is XCDR2, a positional binary format; there is no "spec casing" for JSON to violate).
- **Topic naming**: `tms/{device_id}/{snake_slug}` vs. the IDL's bare CamelCase, no-device-segment names (A.8.6, D.3) — a documented, reversible bridge rule.
- **Sequence-bound narrowings**: several `heapless` bounds are narrowed below the IDL `MAXLEN` for the MCU's 64 KB SRAM budget (e.g. port-measurement sequences 4 vs. `MAX_PORTS`=64) — emit-safe, decode-side-truncating, each documented at its type definition.
